connections.why: Manipulating equations underpins finding lines and circles in coordinate geometry
Algebraic manipulation is needed to work with series and the binomial expansion
Integration is the reverse process of differentiation
Differentiation operates on the polynomial functions studied in algebra
Calculus is later extended to the trigonometric functions
Velocity and acceleration are derivatives of displacement with respect to time
Consistent units and modelling assumptions are needed before analysing motion
Newton's laws explain the forces that produce the motion described by kinematics
Samples provide the data that is then presented and interpreted
Summarising data motivates modelling it with statistical distributions
Probability theory underlies the binomial and other distributions
AS algebra is extended to partial fractions and the modulus function at A2
Coordinate geometry is extended to parametric equations at A2
AS trigonometry is extended with radians and compound-angle formulae
Basic differentiation is extended with the chain, product and quotient rules
Standard integration is extended to substitution and integration by parts
Advanced integration techniques reverse the advanced rules of differentiation
Numerical methods approximate integrals that cannot be found exactly
Constant-acceleration motion is extended to calculus-based motion and projectiles
Forces are extended to their turning effects in the study of moments
Calculus methods are applied to model variable-acceleration motion
Discrete distributions are extended to the continuous normal distribution
The normal distribution is used as a model in hypothesis testing
Basic probability is extended to conditional probability at A2
